false_positives: MINE: my first full-page palette sweep reported 9,554 non-gold saturated pixels. With --disable-lcd-text --disable-font-subpixel-positioning --force-color-profile=srgb the same sweep returns 1. The 9,553 were Chrome LCD subpixel text fringing (mirrored rgb(83,34,10)/rgb(10,34,83) pairs on glyph stems, identical y-ranges). Any future palette probe that screenshots text on this site MUST disable LCD text or it will manufacture this finding again.

MINE: getComputedStyle(pill).display returns 'block', and t_w1_rev1's literal G-MV1 check says display:inline-block. That is NOT a regression — the served CSS declares inline-block and .minivic-launcher is display:flex, so CSS blockifies the flex item. A test asserting the computed value equals 'inline-block' would fail on correct code; assert the declared rule, or assert !== 'none'.
MINE: I first dismissed the OG-image chroma as the same subpixel artefact. I tested that hypothesis (cubic downsample) and it failed — the blue ground is real. Filed as G-OG1 rather than dropped.
